uncited: Uncertainty Loss Parameters are hyperparameters that weight distinct components of an uncertainty-aware regularization objective, balancing fidelity against confidence calibration in differentiable volume rendering.

Unlike sibling methods that model noise distributions directly (e.g., [Uniform and Gaussian Noise Models](5127-uniform-and-gaussian-noise-models.md)), these parameters control the trade-off between minimizing prediction error and penalizing over-confident predictions, ensuring the network learns to express uncertainty where data is sparse or ambiguous.
*   **Input:** Rendered predictions, ground truth values, and predicted uncertainty values $\delta_{c_i}$ for each pixel/ray sample.

detail: supported

This directly supports the claim that these parameters were introduced to handle the difficulty of shallow networks predicting absolute uncertainty.
